name: Kinism
summary: Kinism is a Christian racial and ethnic separatism, concentrated in the Reformed world, holding that God ordained the races and that believers have a moral duty to preserve those divisions. Its writers oppose interracial marriage, defend racial separation in families, churches and (in the newer strands) the nation, and treat racial differences as real and largely permanent. Adherents differ on how far separation extends and whether any race is superior.
scope: The profile represents the self-described kinist and 'Christian race realist' strand as its critics (Dunson, Reasnor, Ehrett) define it: the belief that God ordained races and that it is a duty to preserve those divisions, in marriage, church and nation. The primary texts are Michael Spangler's Christian Race Realism series (2024), whom the defining sources name as a kinist proponent and who accepts the name. Strand differences (weak and strong kinists, national versus ecclesiastical separation) are noted where they show; Christian Identity and its white-only salvation are excluded, as Dunson and Ehrett's descriptions do not include them. Most answers rest on one leading author because the movement has no founding document.
